title: Chapter 1 – Introduction to the Human Body
notes: Anatomy studies structure; Physiology studies function.
Levels of organization: chemical → cellular → tissue → organ → system → organism.
Eleven systems: integumentary, skeletal, muscular, nervous, endocrine, cardiovascular, lymphatic/immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive.
Basic life processes include metabolism, responsiveness, movement, growth, differentiation, reproduction.
Homeostasis: dynamic balance of internal conditions maintained by neural and endocrine regulation.
Negative feedback reduces a deviation (e.g., body temperature regulation).
Positive feedback amplifies a deviation (e.g., oxytocin in labor).
Anatomical position: standing, facing forward, arms at sides, palms forward, feet flat.
Directional terms: superior/inferior; anterior/posterior; medial/lateral; proximal/distal; superficial/deep.
Planes: sagittal (midsagittal/parasagittal), frontal (coronal), transverse (horizontal), oblique.
Dorsal body cavity: cranial + vertebral canal.
Ventral body cavity: thoracic (pleural, pericardial, mediastinum) + abdominopelvic.
Serous membranes: parietal vs visceral layers; pericardium, pleura, peritoneum reduce friction.
Abdominopelvic regions (9) and quadrants (4) standardize location descriptions.
Aging reduces homeostatic efficiency; increases disease susceptibility.
Medical imaging overview: X‑ray, CT, MRI, PET, ultrasound—different strengths and use cases.
Extracellular fluid (ECF) surrounds cells and its composition is tightly regulated.
Feedback loop components: receptor, control center, effector.
Prone vs supine positions reference body orientation when reclining.
In quadrupeds, 'ventral' corresponds to inferior; in humans, anterior.
Membranes in thoracic cavity: pleura (lungs) and pericardium (heart).
Retroperitoneal organs lie posterior to peritoneum (e.g., kidneys).
Homeostatic imbalance can lead to disorder/disease or death if severe.
Regional names (e.g., cephalic, brachial, femoral) provide precise references.
Thoracic cavity separated from abdominopelvic by diaphragm.
Mediastinum contains heart, trachea, esophagus, major vessels (pericardial cavity within).
Serous fluid lubricates organ movement within cavities.
Medical imaging: CT = cross‑sectional X‑ray; MRI = magnetic fields; PET = metabolic activity.
Aging impact example: decreased skin elasticity; slower tissue repair.
